device.help: Which radio. The simulated transponder needs no hardware and is the default.

plutoUri.help: libiio URI: ip:192.168.2.1 (Pluto over USB), ip:pluto.local, ip:<address> (Pluto+, LibreSDR), usb:<bus>.<dev>.<n>.

soapyArgs.help: SoapySDR device arguments for a receive-only SDR, e.g. driver=airspy.

sampleRate.help: Complex sample rate shared by receive and transmit. 1.2 MS/s keeps the transponder in the flat middle of the SDR's filter and lets one TX LO position reach almost the whole band; 600 kS/s costs about a third less CPU but cannot transmit on 2400.210-2400.290 MHz.

converters.help: Converter definitions, in your order: LNBs, upconverters, transverters. Each has a title, a type (down: the radio below the air frequency; up: above), RX only, TX only or RX/TX, RX and TX offsets in Hz, whether it inverts, and the most drive its input takes.

rxConverter.help: The LNB: the converter the receiver works through (9750 MHz for a standard 25 MHz-reference LNB). Beacon lock measures its error; you do not need to know it.

txConverter.help: The converter between the Pluto and 2400 MHz, if any. Usually none: the Pluto transmits on the uplink itself.

rxGainMode.help: Receiver gain control in the SDR.

rxGain.help: Receiver gain when gain control is manual.

rxCorr.help: Receive error: how far high every signal appears. Beacon lock maintains it; persisted so the next start begins close.

txCorr.help: Correction added to the uplink so our signal lands where the VFO says. TX lock maintains it.

txCorrTrusted.help: txCorr came from a TX lock (or a GPS-LNB prediction), so the first search can be narrow.

rigTxCorr.help: Correction added to the external radio's uplink (its reference and the upconverter's LO error together), kept apart from txCorr, which is the SDR's. TX lock maintains it from a carrier.

rigTxCorrTrusted.help: rigTxCorr came from a TX lock, so the first search can be narrow.

rxCorrHand.help: rxCorr was last set by the operator (typed, nudged or click-to-lock), not found by beacon lock's own search. The GPS-locked LNB's transmit prediction never uses such a value.

beaconMode.help: Beacon lock. Auto tracks a beacon and corrects the receive frequency continuously. Hold stops tracking and keeps the correction exactly as it is (a fading beacon, or your own overs). Manual: no tracking; set rxCorr by hand. In Hold and Manual nothing follows the LNB's drift.

beacon.help: Beacon to lock to. The middle BPSK beacon is GPS-referenced and mid-band; the lower F1A beacon is the fallback (and is used automatically when the chosen one is not heard).

beaconSearchHz.help: How far either side of the expected position to search for a beacon. Unmodified LNBs need tens of kHz.

txLock.help: Find our own signal in the downlink while transmitting and correct txCorr.

lnbGpsLocked.help: The LNB has a GPS/reference-locked oscillator. Then the beacon error is mostly the SDR's own reference, and a first txCorr is predicted from it before ever keying.

mmbDecode.help: Receive AMSAT-DL's multimedia beacon (10489.995 MHz: bulletins, pictures, DX-cluster spots, transponder spectra) in the background, from the wide receive signal, whatever you are tuned to. About half a per cent of one core on a laptop.

midTextDecode.help: Decode the middle beacon's text (10489.750 MHz, 400 bit/s BPSK: DK0SB's K, L, M and N message blocks) in the background, whatever you are tuned to. Needs beacon lock, or a receive correction within a few hundred hertz.

kgstvDecode.help: Receive KG-STV pictures (10489.6249 MHz USB: 320x240, about two minutes each, one 16x16 block at a time) in the background, whatever you are tuned to. Pictures of 50 blocks or more are saved.

skimDecode.help: Find and name every signal on the transponder in the background, whatever you are tuned to: SSB voices with their dial measured, CW, data, the beacons and the FT8 windows (the Band view, and marks on the wide scope).

skimBudget.help: The most of one processor core the band skimmer may use. Less only means SSB dials are measured more slowly; receiving is never held up.

rttSec.help: Satellite round trip (about 0.24-0.28 s depending on where you are).

levelMode.help: Own-signal level against the beacon: manual warns only; limit trims TX gain down when we are less than the margin below the beacon; auto also raises it back up (never above the ceiling).

levelMarginDb.help: How far below beacon level our downlink should sit.

txRadio.help: What transmits. The SDR (the Pluto) is keyed by OpenHamShack QO-100 NB; an IC-9700 is keyed only on the radio itself - OpenHamShack QO-100 NB tunes it, follows it, shows and corrects where it lands, and never keys it.

civPort.help: The IC-9700's USB serial port: COM5 (Windows), /dev/ttyUSB0 or /dev/serial/by-id/... (Linux), or socket://host:port for a network serial port.

civBaud.help: CI-V speed. The IC-9700's CI-V USB Baud Rate is Auto by default, which follows this.

civAddress.help: The radio's CI-V address (the IC-9700's default is A2h).

rigctldHost.help: The computer rigctld runs on (127.0.0.1: this one).

rigctldPort.help: rigctld's TCP port (4532 unless started with -t).

rigTxConverter.help: The IC-9700's upconverter to 2400 MHz, from the converter list. Required, and deliberately without a default: a guessed LO would put the uplink somewhere else entirely. An inverting (high-side) one turns the radio's USB into LSB and runs its knob the other way; OpenHamShack QO-100 NB converts.

rigIfBand.help: The IC-9700 band feeding the upconverter.

rigPollMs.help: How often the radio is asked its frequency and whether it is transmitting: the delay before the TX marker follows its knob and before receive audio mutes.

rigRxFollows.help: Turning the radio's knob moves the receive dial too, as on a transceiver. Off: it moves only the transmit dial (split).

rigFmToSsb.help: When the radio is found in FM, which the narrowband transponder does not carry, switch it to SSB (USB on air), between overs. Off: NB never changes the radio's mode, and only warns.

rigAudio.help: Receive audio while the radio transmits. Mute stops your microphone hearing your own downlink from the speaker; the scopes, locks and level measurement carry on regardless.

rigAudioLowerDb.help: How far 'Lower' turns receive audio down while the radio transmits.

split.help: Transmit on txVfo instead of following the receive dial.

txVfo.help: Transmit dial (downlink) when split is on.

freedvMode.help: FreeDV waveform. 700D is the robust choice heard on QO-100; 1600 and 2020 sound better on a strong signal. Only those the installed libcodec2 can open are usable (caps lists them).

hsSpeed.help: HSmodem speed, sending and receiving: 1200 and 2400 BPSK, 3000-4800 QPSK, 5500-7200 8APSK. Both stations must use the same. 4410 (QPSK) is HSmodem's QO-100 standard; the faster ones need a stronger signal.

amWidth.help: AM filter, either side of carrier.

rfGain.help: Fixed audio gain when AGC is off.

nbThreshold.help: Blank samples this many times the mean level.

nr.help: Noise reduction (WDSP's NR2) on what you hear in USB, LSB, CW and AM. Decoders always get the audio without it.

nrStrength.help: How far noise reduction may pull the noise down: 0 % leaves the audio untouched, 100 % up to 40 dB.

txGain.help: SDR transmit gain. Cannot exceed txGainCeiling.

txFilterHi.help: Transmit audio high edge. The occupied width (high - low) may not exceed 2.7 kHz.

pttMode.help: How the UI's space bar keys (UI-side).

txGainCeiling.help: The most transmit gain any control can set.

modeAutoTune.help: Picking a mode with a usual operating frequency (FT8, FT4, CW ...) tunes there, unless the dial is already in its usual place or the radio is keyed (UI-side: Engine.set_mode_tuned).

keyerRepeat.help: Send a voice memory again and again, keyerRepeatSec after each ends, until PTT, Esc or a retune.

keyerRepeatSec.help: Voice keyer: the pause between repeats, listening for a reply.

deadAirSec.help: Voice modes: unkey after this long with no microphone audio.

watchdogSec.help: Unkey if the user interface stops servicing the engine for this long.

zoomPan.help: Zoom scope centre relative to the receive dial.

audioBackend.help: null runs with no sound card (headless, tests).

audioIn.help: Microphone device name; empty for the system default.

audioOut.help: Speaker device name; empty for the system default.

audioOut2.help: Optional second output carrying receive audio to other software (e.g. a loopback device).

simRxErrorHz.help: Simulated LNB error at start: how far high everything appears.

simDriftHz.help: Size of the simulated LNB's slow wander.

simDriftSec.help: Timescale of the simulated LNB's wander.

simUlErrorHz.help: Simulated SDR transmit error: where our signal really goes, relative to where we aim it.

simRefGainDb.help: Transmit gain at which our simulated downlink equals the beacon.

stationCountry.help: The station's country (a DXCC entity's prefix, e.g. GM, EA8, K). Empty: worked out from your callsign - the prefix's country when you sign EA8/GM4BRI.

licence.help: The licence whose conditions the transmit guard enforces. auto: the station country's, where one is written; custom: the segments and power limits you enter yourself.

licenceClass.help: Your licence class, within the licence in force. There is no default: until you choose one, transmit is refused (receiving works).

stationConditions.help: Your answers to the licence's questions about where the station is (near an excluded area, notified an authority...), by the licence's own keys. An unanswered one takes the licence's default, the restrictive side.

customLicence.help: Your own licence, for a country whose rules are not written into OpenHamShack: each segment's lower and upper edge (Hz), most power and its unit (PEP, mean, ERP, EIRP), and whether satellite uplinks are allowed there. Used when Licence is 'custom'.

dxCall.help: The station being worked in FT8/FT4, for the decoder's a-priori passes; empty for none.

ft8Decoder.help: Automatic decodes with OpenHamShack's own decoder, a port of WSJT-X 2.7.0's, and falls back to WSJT-X's jt9 if it is missing or fails. WSJT-X's jt9 puts jt9 first. Whichever is not decoding checks the other's work, where both are installed.

recLimitMin.help: Stop an IQ recording by itself after this many minutes (0: only when you stop it). At 1.2 MS/s a minute takes about 290 MB.

playLoop.help: Start an IQ recording again from the beginning when it ends.

checkUpdates.help: Look for a new version when the program starts and once a day while it runs. The check fetches one small signed file from the program's website and sends nothing about you or this computer. Off: only Help › Check for updates… looks.

pskReporter.help: Send the callsigns you decode in FT8, FT4, Q65 and JS8 to PSKReporter every five minutes: their call, frequency, mode, signal report and grid, with your callsign, locator and this program's name.

simSignals.help: Populate the simulated band with other stations.

simRealtime.help: Pace the simulator to real time (tests turn this off to run faster).

running.help: The engine has the device open and is receiving.

txSource.help: What is keying: ptt, send:<mode>, tune, voice:<n> (voice memory n).

simWhy.help: Why the open device is the simulator, as a sentence for the operator ('' when it is not, or nothing is open).

simFallback.help: The simulator is standing in for a radio that was asked for and could not be had (simWhy says why).

txBlocked.help: Why keying here would be refused right now ('' = it would not).

station.help: Where the station is and the licence in force (ohscore/countries.py InForce.info): entity, region, country, regime, its classes, why transmit is locked when no licence is in force, and notes (abroad, CEPT, QO-100's footprint).

txWarning.help: The transmit card's one standing warning: {key, level, text} of the most important transmit condition now ({} = none). Engine.tx_warn / tx_clear.

rxDial.help: Downlink the receiver is demodulating (vfo + RIT).

txDial.help: Downlink our transmission is meant to land on (txVfo or vfo, + XIT).

txUl.help: Uplink we are aiming at, including txCorr.

segment.help: Bandplan segment under the receive dial.

rxLock.help: Beacon lock: searching, locked, lost (Auto), hold, manual; off before the radio starts.

rxWindow.help: How far either side the beacon search is looking, Hz: +-2 kHz around the correction held first, then beaconSearchHz.

rxReject.help: The last signal beacon lock looked at and refused as not a beacon, and why.

rxErr.help: Last measured beacon error after correction, Hz.

txLockState.help: TX lock: idle, searching (own signal not yet found this over), landed (found txErr off the dial; correcting), locked.

txConfidence.help: Peak-to-noise of the last own-signal measurement.

ownDl.help: Where our own signal was last seen landing (corrected downlink, dial frequency).

vsBeacon.help: Own downlink level relative to the beacon, dB (None until measured).

txPpm.help: txCorr as parts per million of the uplink.

rigLink.help: External transmitter link: off, connecting, ok, lost, error.

rigError.help: Why the external transmitter link is not working, or what it refused.

rigFreq.help: The external radio's own frequency (its IF band), Hz.

rigKeyed.help: The external radio is transmitting (read from it; NB never keys it).

rigMode.help: The external radio's mode on air (after an inverting upconverter).

rigAimDl.help: Downlink the external radio is aimed at, rigTxCorr taken out.

rigTxBlocked.help: Why NB would not transmit where the external radio is aimed (advisory: NB cannot stop it being keyed).

mmbState.help: Multimedia beacon receiver: off, searching, receiving, error (or why it is unavailable).

mmbMer.help: Multimedia beacon decode quality: modulation error ratio of its symbols, dB.

mmbFrames.help: Multimedia beacon frames decoded since the radio started.

mmbLost.help: Multimedia beacon frames that came and did not decode.

mmbLast.help: When the last multimedia beacon frame decoded (Unix time; 0: none yet).

mmbFreq.help: How far the multimedia beacon is from 10489.995 MHz after rxCorr, Hz.

mmbCpu.help: The multimedia beacon receiver's share of one core, per cent.

midTextState.help: Middle beacon text receiver: off, searching (for its carrier), tracking (carrier found, no block for a minute), receiving, error.

midTextSnr.help: Middle beacon text decode quality: its symbols' SNR, dB (0 while searching).

midTextFrames.help: Middle beacon text blocks decoded since the radio started.

midTextLost.help: Middle beacon text blocks whose sync was heard and which did not decode.

midTextLast.help: When the last middle beacon text block decoded (Unix time; 0: none yet).

midTextFreq.help: How far the middle beacon is from 10489.750 MHz after rxCorr, Hz, as its decoder has it.

kgstvState.help: KG-STV picture receiver: off, listening, receiving (a frame decoded in the last 30 s), error.

kgstvFrames.help: KG-STV frames decoded since the radio started (picture blocks, callsigns, end frames).

kgstvLost.help: KG-STV frames whose sync was heard and which did not decode.

kgstvLast.help: When the last KG-STV frame decoded (Unix time; 0: none yet).

kgstvCall.help: The callsign the last KG-STV station sent ('' until one has).

kgstvFreq.help: How far the KG-STV signal's centre is from 10489.6264 MHz after rxCorr, Hz (0 unless receiving).

skimSignals.help: Band skimmer: entries on its list heard in the last 20 s (a calling window counts once).

skimExact.help: Band skimmer: SSB stations among them whose dial auto-tune has measured.

skimCpu.help: Band skimmer: its share of one core over the last 10 s, per cent.

skimLevel.help: Band skimmer: 0 uses every spectrum frame; 1 and 2 every second and fourth, when the spectrum alone costs more than half of skimBudget.

skimLooks.help: Band skimmer: looks at signals (a voice's dial, a narrow signal's keying) finished in the last minute.

skimDropped.help: Band skimmer: receive blocks it fell too far behind to take, since it started.

dishTone.help: Dish alignment: a tone that rises with the middle beacon's SNR, in place of the receive audio.

dishPhone.help: Dish alignment: serve the phone page (the same numbers and a tone) to this network while the tool is open.

dishPort.help: Dish alignment: the phone page's port.

dishOpen.help: Dish alignment is open (transmit is refused meanwhile).

dishSnr.help: Dish alignment: the middle beacon's SNR in 2.5 kHz, dB (None: not measured).

dishBest.help: Dish alignment: the best SNR since it opened or was reset, dB.

dishRise.help: Dish alignment: the transponder's noise over the noise beside it, dB (None: no room beside it at this sample rate).

dishWhere.help: Dish alignment: where the beacon was measured (where beacon lock has it, or the strongest signal near where it should be).

dishGain.help: Dish alignment: what it did to the receive gain, and that it is restored.

dishUrls.help: Dish alignment: the phone page's addresses, comma-separated ('' when off).

dishPhoneError.help: Dish alignment: why the phone page could not start.

cpu.help: Receive thread's own CPU time (time.thread_time()) as a fraction of real time.

cpuWait.help: Extra wall-clock time a receive block took beyond its own CPU time - waiting for the GIL or the OS scheduler, not doing work. High while cpu stays low means receive is starved rather than busy.

overruns.help: Receive blocks the engine fell behind on.

audio.help: Audio status: devices, rates, buffer fill.

modes.help: Per mode: whether it can decode/encode here, or the sentence saying what to install.

error.help: Why the engine is not running, if it is not.

recFile.help: The recording's .sigmf-data file (the last one, once it has stopped).

recSeconds.help: Seconds of IQ in the recording.

recBytes.help: Bytes of IQ written to the recording so far.

recDropped.help: Samples the recording lost because the disk could not keep up.

playing.help: An IQ recording is being played instead of the radio (start_playback).

playUtc.help: When the sample being played was recorded (UTC, seconds since 1970).

playEnded.help: The recording has been played to its end (and is not looping).

autoBusy.help: What is listening to the receive channel now: tune (auto-tune), audio (best audio), or '' for nothing.

autoHeard.help: Seconds of the station auto-tune or best audio has heard so far (while autoBusy).

autoTune.help: What the last auto-tune did: how far it moved the dial (or RIT) and what it measured.

autoTuneRefused.help: Why the last auto-tune refused to move anything ('' when it did).

autoAudio.help: What best audio last measured and chose, in one line.

autoAudioWhy.help: Best audio's reason for each choice, one line per setting.

autoAudioRefused.help: Why the last best audio changed nothing ('' when it applied).

ft8DecoderInUse.help: The decoder FT8/FT4 decodes are coming from: ohsdigi, jt9, or 'jt9 (ohsdigi failed)' after a fallback; '' in other modes.
